paper_metadata.title: An ultra-high temperature Pt-15Ir-3Hf-0.5Y alloy with high hardness and tensile strength achieved by hot rolling and ageing treatment

The mixture with the desired composition was melted and alloyed in a high vacuum arc-melting furnace. The furnace was evacuated to 5 × 10^-3 Pa during smelting process to minimize evaporation and oxidation losses. To enhance the homogeneity, the ingot was flipped over and re-melted 4 – 6 times. The last melting step was completed by furnace cooling while the surface of melt looked homogeneous. And then a button ingot with a thickness of about 6.5 mm and a diameter of 20 mm was fabricated successfully.
In order to obtain high-quality alloy sheets, the hot rolling process at 1000 °C was done on the ingot. The single-pass reduction was set as 5 – 10 %, and the final thickness was reduced to 1.5 mm.
After hot rolling the as-cast and as-hot-rolled samples were aged at 600 °C, 700 °C, 800 °C and 900 °C for 10 h.
After ageing at 700 °C for 10 h, as-cast and as-hot-rolled samples had the highest hardness of 386 HV and 443 HV, respectively.
After ageing treatment (700 C/10 h), the hardness of as-cast and hot-rolled samples are increased by 54 HV and 57 HV, respectively.

evidence.section: 3.3 Microstructure after hot rolling and ageing
evidence.quote: After being hot-rolled at 1000 °C, the microstructure comprises refined and elongated matrix and secondary phases (Fig. 8 a). And the secondary phases also are elongated and fragmented (Fig. 8 b). From the elemental maps shown in Fig. 8 (c-d), these secondary phases are rich in Y. It is deduced that these precipitates are Pt5Y.

And the hardness of as-cast Pt-15Ir-3Hf is 302 HV, which is 130 HV higher than that of the as-cast Pt-15Ir alloy (172 HV). The Hf addition should contribute to this part of hardness, through nanocluster strengthening.
